item.title: Do we ever really say goodbye? On grief and spores.
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description: As a youngster, I used to enjoy stomping down on mushrooms growing in our yard. Sometimes, when I jumped on them particularly ferociously, I could see some sort of powder fly out. Years later, I learned that the flying powder was spores. Spores are one way that nature keeps things alive. It’s like Nature’s filing system. When I stomped on those mushrooms, the powder from under the mushroom’s head and gills generated those puff-clouds, which were then carried off by the breeze into the world.

item.title: The Gossamer Cloak
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description: I beg you tp keep reading for just a minute. This coming week NASA plans to send three projects into space. One of them is the Carruthers Geocorona Observatory. This mission wants to better understand our outer atmosphere. This knowledge will help us understand changes that occur in the area just before we get to “outer space.” Scientists call this the geocorona. Scientists love big words. And, Of course, they need a very specific definition they all know and understand.

item.title: Your ego is essential
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description: Don’t be afraid of your ego The ego is something we can’t see. But, even though we can’t see it, we can observe it in our own lives every day. Our fears, awareness of self, concerns about what the future holds, and what other people are getting are all evidence of our egos at work. We are defensive, afraid to apologize, and afraid to speak up because of our egos. That doesn’t mean the ego is bad.

item.title: Beliefs Worth Examining
item.author: worldwide@worldwidestew.com (Michael Davis)
item.description: What would your belief system - your religion and politics, for example - have to do to cause you to reject it? It’s a question for our ideology-driven times. Decades ago I believed in almost every facet of the Christian Nationalist dream, including their beliefs about sexuality. I ignored the human experience, following ideology instead. Then, as a chaplain in training, I sat by a gay man who lost his partner moments before.
